description: A hospital can transport their patients either using a type II ambulance or hospital van. The hospital needs to transport 320 patients every day. A type II ambulance is mounted on a truck-style chassis and can move 20 patients every shift and costs the hospital (including gas and salary) $820. A hospital van can move 15 patients and costs the hospital $550 every shift. The hospital can have at most 60% of shifts be hospital vans due to union limitations of the type II ambulance drivers. How many of shift using each type of vehicle should be scheduled to minimize the total cost to the hospital?

NumPatients.definition: Number of patients to be transported daily

CapacityAmbulance.definition: Capacity of a Type II ambulance in terms of patients per shift

CostAmbulance.definition: Cost of a Type II ambulance per shift

CapacityVan.definition: Capacity of a hospital van in terms of patients per shift

CostVan.definition: Cost of a hospital van per shift

MaxVanShiftsPercent.definition: Maximum percentage of shifts that can be hospital vans

objective.description: "The goal is to minimize the total daily transportation cost of operating type II ambulances and hospital vans."

constraints.description: 20 * (Number of ambulance shifts) + 15 * (Number of van shifts) >= NumPatients
Number of van shifts <= MaxVanShiftsPercent * (Number of ambulance shifts + Number of van shifts)
Number of ambulance shifts >= 0, Number of van shifts >= 0
Number of ambulance shifts and Number of van shifts are integers

AmbulanceShifts.definition: Number of shifts using Type II ambulances

VanShifts.definition: Number of shifts using hospital vans
